entry.title: Research an account before outreach
entry.summary: Connect account history and recent signals into a focused first-call brief.
prerequisites: Account name, CRM history, latest annual filing, and previous call notes
Web research access; Salesforce and Google Drive connections or exported records
entry.outcome: A one-page account brief with three relevant conversation openers.

steps.title: Build the brief
steps.prompt: Research [account] using its annual filing, recent news, executive updates, CRM records, and our latest call notes. Write one page covering the business, meaningful changes this quarter, where our offer fits, and three specific first-call openers. Distinguish verified facts from hypotheses and link the evidence. Return a document suitable for the account folder.

steps.title: Make the process reusable
steps.prompt: Turn the research approach and my feedback into reusable account-research instructions. Define the sources, freshness checks, one-page structure, and account-folder naming convention.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare a weekly research run
steps.prompt: Using the target-account list I provide, prepare briefs for the next five accounts with the same method. If a scheduling tool is available, configure a Monday 7 a.m. run in [timezone]; otherwise give me the recurring task instructions without claiming it is scheduled.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Track customer account health
entry.summary: Combine usage, support, sentiment, and success-plan progress into one health assessment.
prerequisites: Usage export, open support tickets, NPS responses, and success plan
Salesforce, Zendesk, and Drive access or equivalent exports
entry.outcome: An evidence-backed health rating and two actions for the week.

steps.title: Assess account health
steps.prompt: Review [account] using the attached usage data, open and recently resolved support tickets, NPS feedback, and success plan. Assign a red, yellow, or green health rating with a concise evidence-based explanation. Recommend the two most useful actions this week, naming an owner where the records identify one. Mark missing or stale evidence.

steps.title: Define a repeatable review
steps.prompt: Document the rating criteria, source checks, and summary format as reusable instructions. Incorporate my corrections so the next review applies the same standards.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Review the customer portfolio
steps.prompt: Apply these criteria to each account in [portfolio]. Produce an individual health summary and one digest of red accounts. Prepare the instructions for a Monday 7 a.m. review in [timezone]; only create a recurring task if scheduling is available.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Create a paid-media performance recap
entry.summary: Turn channel exports into a campaign review, a presentation, and a team digest.
prerequisites: Ad-platform exports, conversion data, campaign brief, and previous recap
Spreadsheet and presentation generation; connected Slack only if publishing is requested
entry.outcome: A recap deck, refreshable analysis, and a concise Slack-ready summary.

steps.title: Build the recap
steps.prompt: Analyze the supplied paid-media data for [campaign and period]. Compare spend, reach, conversions, and pipeline contribution across channels. Explain what improved, what deteriorated, and what to change next. Create a concise recap deck, an analysis table that can be refreshed with the same inputs, and a Slack-ready digest of the three largest movers. Link conclusions to the supporting metrics.

steps.title: Capture the reporting method
steps.prompt: Write reusable reporting instructions with metric definitions, attribution assumptions, source locations, deck structure, and the three-mover digest format.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Set up the next recap
steps.prompt: Define a Monday 8 a.m. refresh in [timezone] using the same campaign sources. Specify where the analysis and deck belong and draft the message for #paid-media. Schedule or publish only through available connected tools; otherwise return the task and message for manual use.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Adapt a lesson for three reading levels
entry.summary: Turn a textbook spread into aligned slides, differentiated readings, and a shared assessment.
prerequisites: Textbook page image or PDF, learning standards, and reading-level requirements
Image reading and document/presentation generation
entry.outcome: An 8-10 slide lesson, three reading handouts, and a three-question exit ticket.

steps.title: Build the lesson set
steps.prompt: Use the attached textbook spread, including its diagrams and sidebars, and the supplied learning standard. Create an 8-10 slide lesson with a simplified diagram, three one-page handouts for below-grade, at-grade, and above-grade readers, and a shared three-question exit ticket. Keep the concepts and assessed standard consistent. List vocabulary simplified in the first version. Return editable slide and document files.

steps.title: Add language support
steps.prompt: Adapt the below-grade handout for English learners with a five-term English-Spanish glossary. Replace the final assessment item with a labeled-diagram question that checks the same concept.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Change the teaching sequence
steps.prompt: Rework the deck to begin with observable outcomes before introducing the underlying categories. Use nine slides and preserve alignment to the same standard.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Reuse the lesson rules
steps.prompt: Apply the agreed reading-level rules and assessment structure to [next textbook spread]. Reuse the standards supplied in this conversation and identify any new concepts that require different treatment.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Repurpose content across channels
entry.summary: Transform one substantial piece into coordinated social, email, and audio content.
prerequisites: Source article, brand voice guide, strong previous examples, and visual references
Google Drive connection or uploaded source files; file generation for exports
entry.outcome: Platform-specific drafts with a consistent brand voice.

steps.title: Create the content set
steps.prompt: Repurpose [source article] into a LinkedIn carousel, a short social thread, a five-email nurture sequence, podcast talking points, and an infographic outline. Use the supplied brand examples to maintain a recognizable voice while adapting structure and length to each channel. Present everything in one navigable review document and supply separate files for each format.

steps.title: Simplify the carousel
steps.prompt: Rewrite the carousel for non-specialists. Lead with useful takeaways, replace unnecessary technical language, and preserve the source meaning.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Match proven email examples
steps.prompt: Compare the nurture sequence with the three successful emails I attach. Revise its phrasing, rhythm, and calls to action to match the actual brand voice.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Explore thread angles
steps.prompt: Offer three versions of the thread: a straightforward explanation, a debatable position, and a contrarian angle. Keep factual claims consistent across all three.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Optimize next quarter's campaign budget
entry.summary: Compare campaign and channel results, then model practical budget shifts.
prerequisites: Campaign-level impressions, clicks, conversions, spend, and segment data
ROI target, lifetime-value assumptions, benchmarks, and budget-shift limit
entry.outcome: A performance dashboard and a justified budget-reallocation recommendation.

steps.title: Analyze performance and reallocate
steps.prompt: Analyze [quarter] campaign data across social, search, and email. Rank campaigns and channels by ROI, acquisition cost, and conversion rate. Compare customer segments using [lifetime-value assumptions]. Recommend the next quarter's allocation within [maximum shift], show the calculations, and distinguish projections from observed results. Deliver an Excel dashboard and a written action plan using [ROI target and benchmark].

steps.title: Standardize earlier reports
steps.prompt: Reformat the attached historical performance reviews into this reporting structure. Preserve their original numbers and findings; flag any metrics that cannot be compared consistently.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Improve exploration
steps.prompt: Add useful trend charts, performance heat maps, and filters to the workbook. Keep metric formulas visible and verify that the visuals reconcile to the source totals.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Evaluate fundraising channel returns
entry.summary: Compare donation channels and event formats to guide the next funding budget.
prerequisites: Two years of revenue, costs, donor counts, and event data by channel and quarter
Next-year budget, ROI definition, and any donor retention data
entry.outcome: A board-ready workbook with channel, event, and investment recommendations.

steps.title: Build the fundraising review
steps.prompt: Use the attached fundraising records to compare email, direct mail, social, sponsorship, and events. Calculate net return, ROI, donor acquisition cost, and year-over-year change with visible formulas. Build an Excel workbook with an executive dashboard, quarterly channel details, event performance, and grow/optimize/restructure recommendations. Identify strong but underfunded channels and show the proposed budget shifts. Reconcile totals before presenting conclusions.

steps.title: Compare event formats
steps.prompt: Compare galas, community events, and smaller donor gatherings by ROI, cost structure, revenue potential, and retention where the data supports it. Use charts to show which formats merit expansion or reduction.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the board brief
steps.prompt: Write a polished two-page brief covering the three largest opportunities, their estimated dollar impact, assumptions, owners, and implementation dates.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Model next year
steps.prompt: Create a quarterly forecast with adjustable channel investment scenarios. Show projected revenue and a variance tracker; explain uncertainty instead of inventing statistical confidence from insufficient data.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Find patterns in customer feedback
entry.summary: Bring support conversations, surveys, and interviews into one traceable theme analysis.
prerequisites: Support conversations, NPS responses, and interview notes for a defined period
Intercom access or an export; spreadsheet generation
entry.outcome: A filterable feedback workbook with priorities, representative quotes, and segment comparisons.

steps.title: Synthesize the evidence
steps.prompt: Analyze the attached support conversations, NPS responses, and interview notes for [period]. Group recurring issues by underlying need, distinguish frequent requests from urgent problems, and recommend priorities with supporting evidence. Create a filterable Excel workbook with theme assignments, original source references, representative quotes, trends, and feature requests. Note where the sample may overrepresent a customer segment.

steps.title: Improve the analysis workbook
steps.prompt: Add clear charts for theme trends, comparison tables, and concise insight callouts. Keep the underlying feedback and source references easy to audit.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Compare customer segments
steps.prompt: For the three leading pain points, compare enterprise and smaller-business customers. Separate differences supported by evidence from gaps in the available segment data.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Save the analysis process
steps.prompt: Document the source collection steps, theme methodology, prioritization criteria, and workbook structure as reusable instructions for the next feedback review.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Triage requests in an IT help channel
entry.summary: Answer from policy, collect missing details, and route unresolved requests to an owner.
prerequisites: IT knowledge base and ownership rules
A channel-connected assistant plus ticketing write access for automated replies and filing; pasted requests support manual triage
entry.outcome: Grounded replies and complete, deduplicated escalation tickets.

steps.title: Define the channel triage workflow
steps.prompt: For each request in [IT help channel], check for an existing duplicate and look for an answer in the connected IT knowledge base. Reply with the relevant policy link or ask for missing details. When an owner's decision is needed, prepare one ticket with the request, context, and correct assignee. Do not grant access or make the approval decision. If channel or ticket access is unavailable, draft the response and ticket from the material I provide.

steps.title: Review routing patterns
steps.prompt: Group the recent requests by recurring issue and owner. Identify unresolved or unrouted items and suggest clarifications to the routing rules.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the weekly digest
steps.prompt: Summarize this week's request count, major themes, and outstanding routing gaps. Include untagged channel messages only if the integration can actually read them. Prepare a Friday 3 p.m. digest in [timezone]; configure recurrence only where scheduling is supported.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Restrict response behavior
steps.prompt: Update the channel instructions so the assistant replies only when directly mentioned. State whether the connected channel supports this setting; otherwise return the exact instruction for the channel administrator.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Answer an ad-hoc business data question
entry.summary: Turn a stakeholder question into traceable SQL, an explanation, and a reusable chart.
prerequisites: Business question, warehouse schema or dbt models, metric definitions, and data dictionary
Read-only warehouse connection, or exported data for local analysis
entry.outcome: A validated query, result table, driver analysis, and dashboard specification.

steps.title: Investigate the question
steps.prompt: Investigate this business question: [for example, why did gross margin decline in EMEA this quarter?]. Use the supplied schema and certified metric definitions to write SQL, explain its joins and filters, and run it only if a read-only warehouse connection is available. Otherwise provide the query and identify the missing results. Analyze supported drivers and supply a chart specification that makes the answer reusable in our dashboard.

steps.title: Document the query workflow
steps.prompt: Capture the metric definitions, query checks, naming conventions, and answer format as reusable instructions for similar stakeholder questions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare incoming-question triage
steps.prompt: Define a workflow for reviewing new requests in [analytics channel], saving the query and draft response for each thread, and holding the answer for my review. Specify the required channel and warehouse permissions before any hourly automation is created.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Explore regression by moving data points
entry.summary: Build intuition for best-fit lines, outliers, and leverage through an interactive experiment.
prerequisites: An environment that can render interactive HTML, or a browser to open a generated HTML file
entry.outcome: A draggable scatterplot with regression comparisons and prediction exercises.

steps.title: Build the experiment
steps.prompt: Create an interactive scatterplot for learning linear regression. Start with a blank plot where I can add and drag points, then update the fitted line immediately. Include controls to reveal residuals and influence so I can see why an outlier changes the fit. Keep the explanation brief and let me experiment. If inline interaction is unavailable, provide a self-contained HTML file.

steps.title: Explain leverage
steps.prompt: Use the points currently in the plot to explain the leverage formula. Show explicitly where horizontal distance from the mean enters the calculation and how it differs from vertical residual size.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Compare a robust fit
steps.prompt: Overlay a robust regression fit on the same points. Let me drag an outlier and compare how both fitted lines respond.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Test my intuition
steps.prompt: Present several scatterplot patterns. Ask me to predict what moving one outlier will do before revealing the resulting fit, then explain any surprise.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Build an internal knowledge assistant
entry.summary: Find cited answers across engineering documentation, repositories, and data ownership records.
prerequisites: Service catalog, glossary, team directory, and documentation access
Confluence and GitHub connections or exports; read-only warehouse access for metric questions
entry.outcome: Reusable answering instructions and a backlog of knowledge gaps.

steps.title: Answer one real question
steps.prompt: Answer [engineering question] using the supplied service catalog and connected documentation, repository, and data sources. Start with the catalog to choose where to look. Cite the exact evidence and name the responsible team when known. If the evidence is missing or contradictory, say what remains unresolved and who can verify it. First produce one useful answer; then turn the approach into reusable internal-assistant instructions.

steps.title: Refine the assistant instructions
steps.prompt: Incorporate my feedback into the source-routing rules, citation requirements, ownership lookup, and uncertainty handling. Include examples of questions that require a human owner.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Track knowledge gaps
steps.prompt: Review the questions and answers provided for [week]. Group unresolved questions by topic and propose an owner for each documentation gap. Prepare a weekly gaps report; only schedule ongoing collection if the required logging and scheduling tools are connected.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Audit visual assets against brand rules
entry.summary: Check image exports for outdated logos, incorrect colors, and missing required copy.
prerequisites: Brand guidelines, required legal copy, and PNG/JPEG asset files
Image inspection; optional live asset URLs, browser access, and Asana connection
entry.outcome: An asset-level compliance report grouped by issue and confidence.

steps.title: Audit the asset folder
steps.prompt: Inspect every supplied PNG and JPEG against [brand guidelines] and [required-copy document]. Check logo versions, specified colors, and the presence and readable size of required copy. Group findings by violation type. For each, report filename, expected rule, observed value, evidence, and confidence. Separate uncertain visual estimates from exact file metadata and count assets with no detected issues.

steps.title: Check published versions
steps.prompt: Use [asset URL mapping] to inspect the live page for each high-confidence finding. Report whether the published asset still shows the issue or appears corrected; identify pages you cannot access.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare correction tasks
steps.prompt: Prepare one Asana task per high-confidence issue with the asset owner, filename, relevant rule, and proposed correction. Create tasks only when the project and write access are available.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Repeat the audit
steps.prompt: Write reusable brand-audit instructions and a Friday 2 p.m. schedule specification in [timezone], including the asset location and summary destination. Configure the recurring run only if the necessary file, scheduling, and messaging connections are available.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Turn brand guidelines into reusable instructions
entry.summary: Translate design tokens and voice rules into a consistent generation standard.
prerequisites: Brand guidelines, color and spacing tokens, typography rules, and voice examples
Figma and Notion access or exported documentation
entry.outcome: A reusable brand instruction set, a one-page reference, and a change log.

steps.title: Encode the brand rules
steps.prompt: Read the supplied brand documentation and design-system references. Create reusable on-brand instructions covering exact color tokens, typography, spacing, voice, and prohibited patterns. Explain briefly why each prohibited pattern conflicts with the system. Include a checklist that can be applied to generated copy and interfaces, and flag conflicts between sources.

steps.title: Refine the instructions
steps.prompt: Apply my feedback to the rules and examples. Preserve the source reference for each requirement and identify any decision that still needs the brand owner.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Create the team reference
steps.prompt: Create a one-page reference explaining what these instructions enforce, with concise examples of compliant and noncompliant choices.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Plan guideline synchronization
steps.prompt: Compare the current brand folder and Figma library with the previous version. Update changed rules and produce a brief changelog. Prepare a Monday 9 a.m. refresh specification in [timezone]; a recurring run requires connected sources and scheduling support.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Make a whiteboard lesson interactive
entry.summary: Show the forces behind an economic diagram instead of only its final intersection.
prerequisites: A whiteboard photo, slide, or description of the lesson
Interactive HTML rendering or a browser for a generated file
entry.outcome: A predict-and-check teaching visual for equilibrium and price controls.

steps.title: Visualize the mechanism
steps.prompt: I am teaching supply and demand equilibrium. Review [my sketch] and suggest a clearer way to explain why price moves toward equilibrium. Build an interactive visual that shows surplus or shortage creating pressure on price, rather than only drawing intersecting curves. Provide a browser-ready HTML version if it cannot run inline.

steps.title: Ask students to predict
steps.prompt: Before showing the resulting price movement, let students predict its direction. Display their prediction beside the actual result and explain the difference.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Explore a demand shock
steps.prompt: Add a demand-spike scenario. Animate the curve shift and let students observe how price and quantity reach the new equilibrium.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Teach price controls
steps.prompt: Reuse the predict-and-check interaction for price floors and ceilings. Show why an imposed price can leave a persistent shortage or surplus.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Build a competitive battlecard library
entry.summary: Combine lost-deal evidence with current competitor research into usable sales guidance.
prerequisites: Closed-lost deal notes with competitor fields for a defined period
CRM export or connection, web research access, and optional brand reference
entry.outcome: A searchable competitor dashboard with grounded objections and talk tracks.

steps.title: Create the battlecards
steps.prompt: Review closed-lost deals from the last six months for [competitors]. Identify loss patterns in the deal notes, then research current competitor sites, reviews, and positioning. Build a compact interactive dashboard with a competitor list and detailed battlecards containing strengths, weaknesses, differentiators, objection responses, and cited evidence. Date time-sensitive claims and distinguish customer perceptions from verified product facts.

steps.title: Practice realistic objections
steps.prompt: Create three sales-call exercises from actual objections in the losses to [competitor]. Include the objection, an evidence-backed response, and likely follow-up questions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Update earlier positioning
steps.prompt: Compare the current evidence for [competitor] with our previous-quarter battlecard. Explain what changed and propose precise updates to the counter-messaging.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Build an interactive bucket-list app
entry.summary: Create a personal experience catalog with saved goals and satisfying interactions.
prerequisites: A browser-capable coding environment
AI recommendations require a separately configured AI integration; the base app works locally
entry.outcome: A working experience browser with a personal list and planning handoffs.

steps.title: Build the experience browser
steps.prompt: Create a polished interactive bucket-list app with categorized life experiences, a browse view, and a saved My List view. Use thoughtful typography, spacing, and restrained selection animations. Seed it with varied experiences and preserve saved choices locally. Make it work on mobile and desktop.

steps.title: Turn a goal into a plan
steps.prompt: Add a Make this happen action to each saved experience. Generate a copyable research prompt containing its name and my notes, asking for practical steps, costs to investigate, and preparation needed.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Suggest an unexpected experience
steps.prompt: Add a recommendation action based on the patterns in my saved list. If an AI integration is configured, use it to suggest one new experience with a reason; otherwise generate a copyable recommendation prompt rather than implying a live AI connection.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Personalize completion
steps.prompt: Add optional first-run name and birthday fields, a personalized header, and an understated age display. When an experience is completed, animate a brief color-matched particle effect and respect reduced-motion preferences.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Prepare a daily cross-tool briefing
entry.summary: Connect dashboard alerts, conversations, and tasks into one morning view.
prerequisites: Slack and Notion access or exported messages and tasks
Access to the team dashboard; browser capability if it is not available through a connector
entry.outcome: A prioritized briefing with context, blockers, and linked evidence.

steps.title: Build the morning briefing
steps.prompt: Prepare my morning briefing from [Slack channels], [Notion workspace], and [team dashboard URL]. Lead with urgent or deteriorating dashboard signals, then full threads mentioning me, relevant discussions I am missing, and tasks due this week with blockers. For urgent items, explain the people involved, prior discussion, and unresolved decision. Link evidence and identify any inaccessible source.

steps.title: Investigate an alert
steps.prompt: Investigate [dashboard alert] using its related conversations and tasks. Explain the timeline, contributing factors, owners, and the next unresolved action.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Draft a contextual reply
steps.prompt: Draft a reply to [thread] using the full context. Confirm the intended next step while clearly flagging [dependency]. Keep the message ready for my review.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Connect one topic across tools
steps.prompt: Find what has been discussed about [topic] across messages, task records, and dashboard information. Reconcile decisions, dates, and open questions into one brief.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Compare business growth with economic indicators
entry.summary: Combine revenue from board decks with matching public macroeconomic series.
prerequisites: Quarterly board decks with revenue figures
Access to FRED data or downloaded series; chart and presentation generation
entry.outcome: A sourced comparison chart, short interpretation, and board slide.

steps.title: Build the comparison
steps.prompt: Extract revenue for [four quarters] from the supplied board decks and record the slide supporting each figure. Retrieve matching GDP growth and inflation series from FRED, noting units, frequency, and release dates. Compare our revenue growth with these indicators using aligned periods and clearly labeled axes. Create a chart and concise interpretation without treating correlation as causation.

steps.title: Add more indicators
steps.prompt: Add unemployment and consumer-confidence measures for the same period. Choose a presentation that remains readable despite differing units and explain any series transformation.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Extend the history
steps.prompt: Use the additional archived board decks to extend the comparison to three years. Check that revenue definitions and macroeconomic frequencies remain comparable.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Create a board slide
steps.prompt: Create a single PowerPoint slide with the chart, key figures, source notes, and three useful discussion points. Return it as an editable file.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Build evidence-based customer personas
entry.summary: Group customers by observed behavior and recurring problems across research sources.
prerequisites: Interview transcripts, survey responses, sales notes, and support conversations
HubSpot and Intercom access or exported records
entry.outcome: Explorable personas with journeys, quotations, and product opportunities.

steps.title: Identify behavioral personas
steps.prompt: Analyze the supplied customer research and connected CRM/support records. Find customer groups based on behavior, goals, and problems rather than assumed demographics. Create an interactive persona overview with journeys, frustrations, actual attributed quotes, and evidence for each grouping. Explain coverage gaps and distinguish strong patterns from tentative segments.

steps.title: Write the executive report
steps.prompt: Summarize the segments, their needs, journey friction, and product-roadmap implications in a shareable report. Tie recommendations back to the research evidence.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Assess revenue opportunity
steps.prompt: Compare which segment could offer the greatest revenue opportunity if its experience improved. Use available commercial data, show assumptions, and describe the product changes required.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Find support-driven quick wins
steps.prompt: For the largest supported segment, identify its most common support themes and propose product changes that address the top three. Include examples and expected impact where measurable.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Build an investment scenario model
entry.summary: Connect company financials, peer valuations, and deal assumptions into a reviewable model.
prerequisites: Company financials, deal terms, investment-committee template, and comparable-company data
Daloopa, S&P Global, and document-store access or equivalent supplied exports
entry.outcome: A formula-driven investment workbook with scenarios, sensitivities, and risk analysis.

steps.title: Model the investment
steps.prompt: Evaluate [company] using [investment size, entry valuation, holding period, and exit assumption]. Reconcile its historical revenue, margins, customers, and growth from the supplied data. Build an Excel model with base, upside, and downside cases; sensitivities for growth and exit multiple; and a dated peer-comparison table. Examine concentration risk from the largest customers and show how it changes the downside. Use visible formulas and separate sourced facts from assumptions.

steps.title: Draft the committee memo
steps.prompt: Use our supplied committee template to summarize the deal, thesis, modeled returns, principal risks, and a conditional recommendation. Cite the workbook inputs behind key claims.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Challenge the growth path
steps.prompt: Compare the projected growth path with relevant portfolio or public-company trajectories at a similar scale. Explain comparability limits and revise scenarios that lack support.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Check realized exit valuations
steps.prompt: Research comparable transactions from the last 18 months in [revenue range]. Distinguish actual transaction multiples from public trading multiples and explain how they support or challenge our exit assumption.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Create an interactive anatomy explorer
entry.summary: Build a study tool from authoritative anatomical SVGs with consistent identifiers.
prerequisites: Coding environment with npm access and a browser preview
Anatomical reference material to verify explanatory content
entry.outcome: An anatomy reference app with quizzes and companion study materials.

steps.title: Build the anatomy tool
steps.prompt: Build an interactive anatomy explorer using @ebi-gene-expression-group/anatomogram and its homo_sapiens.male.svg and homo_sapiens.brain.svg assets. Embed the SVGs locally. Preserve UBERON IDs, disable ID cleanup, remove hidden visibility, and explicitly set visible fills and strokes. Add clear information tabs and verified explanations. Use warm restrained colors, serif headings, readable body text, and optional sound feedback.

steps.title: Add self-testing
steps.prompt: Create a quiz that describes a structure or function and asks me to select it on the diagram. Track accuracy and identify systems that need more practice.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Expand anatomical coverage
steps.prompt: Add more body systems and a more detailed brain view using appropriate source assets. Keep identifiers and terminology consistent rather than inventing anatomical shapes.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Export study materials
steps.prompt: Generate a printable PDF study guide organized by body system and Anki-compatible flashcards from the same verified content. Keep terminology and clinical examples aligned with the explorer.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Prepare for a sales call
entry.summary: Combine deal history, recent calls, and the action plan into focused meeting preparation.
prerequisites: CRM record, last three call transcripts, and mutual action plan
Calendar access for a daily batch; Salesforce and Drive access or exports
entry.outcome: A call-prep sheet with priorities, asks, objections, and responses.

steps.title: Prepare the call sheet
steps.prompt: Prepare for my meeting with [account] on [date]. Use the CRM record, latest three call transcripts, and mutual action plan to explain deal status and buyer priorities. Recommend two or three specific asks for this call and likely objections with grounded responses. Highlight unresolved commitments and any conflicting information.

steps.title: Make preparation consistent
steps.prompt: Capture our discovery framework, objection-handling principles, and call-sheet format as reusable instructions. Apply my feedback to the examples.

Identify the repository, channel, ownership, and automation capabilities needed before enabling it.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Investigate without changing code
steps.prompt: For [new report], trace the failure to its cause and explain the evidence and reproduction result. Diagnosis only: do not edit files or create a pull request.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Refresh a driver-based financial forecast
entry.summary: Extend actuals into three scenarios and explain the assumptions behind the differences.
prerequisites: Driver model, newly closed actuals, and approved scenario assumptions
Spreadsheet editing; NetSuite or document-store access or exported files
entry.outcome: A four-quarter model and a one-page leadership assumptions memo.

steps.title: Update and compare scenarios
steps.prompt: Reconcile the latest closed actuals with the supplied driver model, then extend the forecast through the next four quarters. Build base, upside, and downside cases using explicit input changes. Save a new workbook copy with separate scenario tabs and working formulas alongside the supplied original; preserve the original unchanged. List every changed assumption and its magnitude, and show the impact on key outputs. Write a one-page plain-language memo explaining what drives the scenario differences and save it beside the new workbook.

steps.title: Save the forecasting method
steps.prompt: Document the driver relationships, input sources, scenario sensitivities, reconciliation checks, and memo structure as reusable instructions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the reforecast cadence
steps.prompt: Define a process that detects newly closed actuals in [forecast folder], creates a refreshed model and scenario memo, and preserves the prior version. Specify the file, spreadsheet, and scheduling capabilities needed for a recurring run.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Draft an organization-specific AI usage policy
entry.summary: Align practical AI use with existing privacy commitments, mission, and oversight.
prerequisites: Organization context, populations served, existing privacy/security policies, and code of ethics
Current authoritative research and relevant jurisdiction; document generation
entry.outcome: A policy draft, public summary, and implementation/training materials.

steps.title: Draft the governance policy
steps.prompt: Draft an AI usage policy for [organization], using its existing privacy policy, ethics code, and work with [beneficiaries]. Research relevant current sector examples with citations. Cover tool approval, risk assessment, oversight, permitted/prohibited data, retention, acceptable uses, human review, training, escalation, bias checks, and transparency. For sensitive services, distinguish administrative support from clinical or beneficiary decisions. Mark unresolved legal/policy choices and create a Word draft plus a concise public Markdown summary.

steps.title: Create staff training
steps.prompt: Develop slides and handouts using realistic organizational scenarios. Explain permitted uses, verification duties, data handling, and a decision tree for when human review or escalation is required.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the board discussion
steps.prompt: Create a board deck covering the reason for the policy, key provisions, implementation timeline, responsible owners, and measurable compliance checks. Identify decisions the board must make.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Explain the policy to donors
steps.prompt: Draft clear donor-facing language for the annual report, website FAQ, and direct questions. Explain actual protections and review practices without claiming safeguards that have not been adopted.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Consolidate project status across tools
entry.summary: Reconcile messages, meetings, and documents into a task tracker with visible blockers.
prerequisites: Project name, reporting period, emails, channel history, documents, and meeting notes
Connected sources or exports; spreadsheet generation
entry.outcome: A source-linked Excel tracker and an executive status brief.

steps.title: Build the task tracker
steps.prompt: Consolidate [project] updates from the last two weeks of email, its team channel, project documents, and meeting notes. For each task, record owner, current status, blockers, blocker age where supported, plans, and source context. Resolve conflicting updates by date and flag unresolved disagreements. Create an Excel tracker with status/priority dropdowns, source comments, and useful visual indicators; do not invent progress percentages.

steps.title: Trace a blocker
steps.prompt: Find every available mention of [blocker] across the sources. Reconstruct its escalation history, decisions, owner, and latest supported status, with timestamps and links.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Brief leadership
steps.prompt: Create a one-page report from the tracker with overall progress using an explicit defensible definition, blocker count, at-risk workstreams, and three items requiring leadership attention. State missing coverage.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Explore gene-expression patterns and pathway evidence
entry.summary: Analyze cell-specific expression differences and compare biological hypotheses with the literature.
prerequisites: Differential-expression or normalized-count files with sample/cell annotations and study design
Computational analysis environment and access to relevant pathway databases and PubMed
entry.outcome: Reproducible plots, enrichment results, and a cited interpretation of known versus uncertain mechanisms.

steps.title: Analyze the selected cell population
steps.prompt: Use the attached adult and pediatric liver dataset, focusing on parenchymal cells rather than the immune-cell analysis. Inspect the study design, annotations, normalization, and available differential-expression results before choosing methods. Create a labeled heatmap and pathway/gene-set enrichment comparison with appropriate multiple-testing treatment. Return the code, parameters, limitations, and testable biological hypotheses rather than causal conclusions.

steps.title: Check extracellular-matrix findings
steps.prompt: Focus on extracellular-matrix and remodeling genes in the pediatric liver results. Search PubMed for relevant evidence and distinguish established developmental roles from uncertain or apparently less-studied associations. Cite the exact studies, verify gene identities, and avoid treating a lack of retrieved literature as proof of novelty.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Build a reusable grant-proposal system
entry.summary: Turn proven organizational material into maintainable modules and funder-specific submissions.
prerequisites: Successful proposals, program descriptions, annual report, outcome data, attachments, and target RFP
Document/spreadsheet generation; Drive and Gmail access only for saving or drafting there
entry.outcome: A modular content library, first proposal, and tracking/budget templates.

steps.title: Build the library and first proposal
steps.prompt: Use the supplied proposals and organizational records to create reusable modules: brief/standard/detailed program descriptions, sourced need statements, organizational capacity, evaluation/results, and an attachment index. Track each module's source and freshness. Assemble a proposal for [target RFP] with its exact page limits, priorities, budget narrative, logic model, and evaluation requirements. Also create a grant/deadline tracker, funder-research template, module-selection guide, formula-based budget template, and submission/follow-up email drafts. Flag missing evidence rather than inventing outcomes.

steps.title: Add new evidence-based modules
steps.prompt: Using this quarter's supplied outcomes, add modules for [new topics, such as recovery work, inclusion, or resilience]. Match the library structure, date the evidence, and avoid introducing unsupported organizational achievements.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Customize a proposal batch
steps.prompt: Prepare separate proposals for [three funders and RFPs] using the same verified library. Tailor framing, metrics, and language to each funder while checking eligibility, limits, budget categories, and attachments independently.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Improve the library from outcomes
steps.prompt: Compare the provided successful and unsuccessful proposals with funder feedback. Identify useful language and weak or stale sections, without treating a small sample as causal proof. Update modules with dated evidence and write a practical guide to the observed patterns.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Reconcile headcount across HR, budget, and payroll
entry.summary: Match people and cost centers to uncover planning and accounting differences.
prerequisites: HR roster, headcount plan, payroll/GL records, and employee/cost-center mappings
Consistent reporting date and definitions of employee, contractor, and budgeted position
entry.outcome: A cost-center reconciliation with categorized exceptions and source references.

steps.title: Reconcile the headcount
steps.prompt: Reconcile [month] headcount across the HR roster, approved plan, and payroll/GL records using employee ID and cost center. Identify unplanned hires, budgeted vacancies, roster records with no payroll, payroll records absent from HR, and contractors classified as employees. Explain effective-date and timing differences separately. Produce a cost-center reconciliation and an exception list linked to the source rows.

steps.title: Save reconciliation rules
steps.prompt: Document the matching keys, cost-center mapping, headcount definitions, timing treatment, and exception categories. Incorporate my corrections into the repeatable review process.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the monthly refresh
steps.prompt: Define a check for a new HR export in [close folder], reconciling it with the corresponding plan and payroll period. Save a dated result without overwriting prior reconciliations; recurring execution requires the appropriate source access and scheduler.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Draft a blameless incident postmortem
entry.summary: Reconstruct the incident timeline and link impact, causes, and actions to evidence.
prerequisites: Incident channel, alert timeline, technical evidence, and postmortem template
Slack/PagerDuty access or exported records
entry.outcome: A reviewable postmortem with timestamps, uncertainty, and action ownership.

steps.title: Reconstruct the incident
steps.prompt: Use [incident channel], alert history, and supplied technical evidence to build a timestamped sequence of events. Summarize customer impact, identify the supported root cause and contributing factors, and draft the postmortem in our template. Cite evidence, separate hypotheses from confirmed causes, and flag gaps. Describe system behavior without blame. Assign action owners only where supported; mark others for assignment.

steps.title: Capture the postmortem standard
steps.prompt: Document the severity definitions, evidence sources, timeline conventions, action format, and blameless-writing rules as reusable instructions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare resolved-incident intake
steps.prompt: Define a weekday 6 p.m. workflow for incidents resolved in the preceding 24 hours. Create one draft per incident with its source timeline and avoid duplicate processing. A live workflow requires alert, channel, file, and scheduling access.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Synthesize interview evidence for a debrief
entry.summary: Show where interviewers agree, where evidence conflicts, and what the panel must resolve.
prerequisites: Completed interviewer scorecards, role rubric, and competency expectations
Authorized access to candidate material; no automated hiring decision is requested
entry.outcome: A neutral debrief brief with competency coverage and three decision questions.

steps.title: Prepare the panel brief
steps.prompt: Synthesize the supplied interview scorecards against the role rubric. Show where the panel agrees and disagrees, distinguish strong behavioral evidence from anecdotes, and identify competencies that were not assessed. Cite the relevant scorecard evidence and propose three questions to resolve in the debrief. Do not recommend hire/no-hire or infer protected characteristics; the decision stays with the panel.

steps.title: Refine the synthesis rules
steps.prompt: Document our rubric, convergence criteria, evidence standard, and missing-coverage flags. Apply my feedback while preserving the separation between evidence synthesis and the panel's judgment.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare complete-scorecard intake
steps.prompt: Define a weekday 9 a.m. check for candidates whose required scorecards are complete. Create a brief in the relevant role folder, preserving access limits and avoiding duplicate drafts. Scheduling requires connected tools.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Check readiness for a product launch
entry.summary: Reconcile launch evidence into an owned checklist and a clear assessment of blockers.
prerequisites: Launch PRD, project epic, go-to-market brief, checklist, and recent team updates
The previous two launch reviews; Linear/Slack/Drive access or exports
entry.outcome: A red/yellow/green readiness brief with lessons from prior launches.

steps.title: Assess launch readiness
steps.prompt: Review the supplied evidence for [launch]. Build a checklist with status, owner, and supporting source for each item. Apply [readiness criteria] to an overall red/yellow/green assessment, name blockers, and separate unknowns from completed work. Compare risks and strengths with lessons from our previous two launches. Do not treat the assessment itself as launch approval.

steps.title: Save the readiness standard
steps.prompt: Capture the checklist, ownership map, status criteria, and prior-launch lessons as reusable launch-review instructions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare launch-week updates
steps.prompt: Define a daily 8 a.m. review during [launch week and timezone], producing a dated checklist and one-line explanation of any overall-status change from yesterday. A recurring run requires current source access and scheduling support.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

entry.title: Draft a structured legal research memo
entry.summary: Organize relevant authority around a precise question and expose unresolved issues.
prerequisites: Legal question, relevant facts, jurisdiction, date, and house memo/citation format
Current authoritative research access such as Thomson Reuters, or supplied source documents
entry.outcome: A cited research draft with a short answer and an authority-led discussion.

steps.title: Research the question
steps.prompt: Research [legal question] for [jurisdiction and date] using available authoritative case law, legislation, and regulatory guidance. Draft a memo with question presented, short answer, discussion grouped by authority, and open issues. Cite every legal proposition and distinguish binding from persuasive authority. Verify currency where tools permit and identify any source or subsequent-treatment check that remains unavailable.

steps.title: Create reusable research instructions
steps.prompt: Document the house format, citation style, jurisdictions, source hierarchy, and currency checks. Include an explicit process for unresolved facts and authorities that require verification.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare research intake
steps.prompt: Define a weekday 9 a.m. process for new requests in [research intake folder], saving a cited draft for each question. Specify the research subscriptions, document access, and scheduling tools required before enabling it.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

Calendar/CRM connector or authenticated browser; CRM write access only for approved saves
entry.outcome: Reviewed activity drafts with next steps and accurate CRM associations.

steps.prompt: Review today's calendar in [timezone] and select external meetings, excluding internal events and cancellations. Draft an activity record with discussion points and next steps for each meeting. Check for existing logs and show all drafts for review before saving anything.

steps.prompt: For [confirmed opportunity], prepare these changes: stage [stage], close date [exact date], and competitor [name]. Show the current and proposed values, then apply only the changes I have approved.
